title: doctor's attachment-drift remedy names a destructive step that sync --to-disk does not take, and render.rs describes the same flag two ways
body:
**FILED AS A STUB AND CLOSED AS ONE. THE BODY BELOW IS RESTORED ARCHAEOLOGY, NOT NEW ANALYSIS** -- transcribed verbatim on 2026-08-31 from `4c04bcb5`, the commit that filed this issue, whose author is the finder. Nothing here is written by the restorer.

dc's own account of why this issue carries no body, in the commit that created it:

> 0164 is the same issue filed without a body, closed as a stub. There is no door to add a body after creation -- issue 0090, which is on wip.md's own list and which I had read this morning.

**`0165` CARRIES THE FINDING THIS STUB DUPLICATES.** dc's statement of it, from the same commit:

> 0165 files the finding vc and I could each only half-establish. doctor's attachment-drift remedy says `sync --to-disk <ID>` writes the store's version over the file and discards the working copy. It does not: `projection` carries no attachment path, and a run with the store holding old text and the file holding new edits left the file dirty afterwards. That run was an accident and it is the only clean experiment either of us had, because a correct `--to-store` then `--to-disk` sequence cannot produce the case. render.rs describes the same flag two ways at :698 and :818, and the remedy sides with the wrong one, so both move together or neither does.

**PROVENANCE:** `4c04bcb5` -- *wb(dc): localfold -- six Decisions entries were one class, and 0165 is the day's finding*.
